key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning produced the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network showed strong shared-learning generalization across the related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a shared multi-output model for efficient learning and an ensemble approach for higher task-specific predictive accuracy in process optimization and quality control.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding responses: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated both approaches using RMSE and R² on the same dataset.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² for all three outputs, including UTS (RMSE 0.0263, R² 0.9863), weld hardness (0.0467, 0.9782), and HAZ hardness (0.1109, 0.8453).
watch_item: Results are dataset-dependent, so stacking may generalize less reliably than MTL if future welding conditions differ or the available training data become sparse.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
